- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates in early part of 30-day horizon (days 1–5); apply +1–2% bias to first 5 days.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2% above recent low for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is high (e.g., 0.4 or above), model often overreacts; apply 1–3% downward correction to forecast for next 5–7 days.
- Model frequently misses upward momentum in 30-day horizon; if last 3–5 days show rising trend, forecast should be 1–3% higher than model for next 5–7 days.
